title: A Funeral for a Frequency
summary: Mast Nine — the listening horn's oldest ear — answered its last true carrier in the spring and has spoken nothing but repeats since. Static-Warden Pem is retiring its brass voice-box to the Drowned Array, where dead frequencies are cairned, and Pem walks the whole way beside the wagon. Ride escort. Slowly. It is a funeral.

objectives.label: Meet Pem at the temple steps — the voice-box rides in state
Escort the voice-box to the Drowned Array — Pem sets the pace; mourners do not outrun the coffin
Seat the voice-box among the patient dead — gently, it rode with its ears open

offer.text: Station. A small death to report. Mast Nine — firstborn of the listening horn, older than the Choir, older than my notebooks — answered its last true carrier in the spring. What leaves it now are repeats: my own weather reports coming home to roost, wearing better diction.

We retire a mast's voice-box to the Drowned Array, where the desert archives anything patient. I will walk the wagon down myself — forty years it listened to me; the last courtesy left is footsteps. Ride escort, station. A funeral with no witnesses is only garbage day.

accept.text: Rules for a mast funeral: no boosting beside the wagon — the voice-box rattles, and it *hates* rattling. If the old call-sign plays once while you ride, that's normal. If it plays slightly *wrong*, that's also normal. We stopped writing that down because the writing was getting upset.

The route is honest: the lamp ring, the rim, the long quiet, the pan edge, and then the cairns, where TALLY-9 keeps its sad arithmetic. Stay near, station. A mourner who outruns the coffin has misunderstood mourners.

Ketch here. Escort speed, kid — that wagon is older than your debt's grandmother. Keep formation loose and kind, and no boosting past the cairns at the far end. The Array has opinions about wakes. I don't mean boat wakes.

complete.text: You heard nothing just now, station. So did I. Two rows of the notebook left blank, on purpose, in respect. … The call-sign came once — a half-step flat. Forty years of weather fiction, and tonight the fiction got the *notes* right and the voice wrong. That is not a malfunction. That is a reply.

REGISTERED: one (1) voice-box, brass, still warm, declined to file cleanly. The Array accepts the patient. This unit has opened a new category of deceased: RETIRED, LISTENING. Condolences are filed in chalk, where they keep better.
Logged: escorted a dead radio to the cemetery for dead radios, walked it in like family, got thanked for the weather by a machine. Best Tuesday I've had.
